title: How Deep Is the Tree
statement:
You are given `root`, the top node of a **binary tree** (every node has a `val`, and a `left` and a `right` child that may be empty). An empty tree is passed as an empty `root`.

Return the **maximum depth**: the number of nodes along the longest path from the root down to a leaf. An empty tree has depth 0. (In the examples a tree is written level by level from the top; `null` marks a missing child.)

hints.nudge: The depth of a tree is related to the depths of its two subtrees. How?
hints.pseudocode:
depth(node): if node is empty: return 0
  return 1 + max(depth(node.left), depth(node.right))
hints.walkthrough: A tree is a root plus two smaller trees, so recursion fits: the depth of an empty tree is 0, and otherwise it is one more than the deeper of the two subtrees. Every node is visited once: O(n) time, and the recursion stack is as deep as the tree (O(h)). A level-by-level traversal (BFS) that counts levels gives the same answer.
